name: Bottleneck

whatIsIt.eli5: Two pattern-finders in a row, plus a shortcut that adds back what came in, so the original is never forgotten.
whatIsIt.simple: Two Conv blocks in a row with an optional shortcut: the input is added to the result. It is the small unit repeated inside C2f, C3 and C3k2.
whatIsIt.engineer: cv1 (k0×k0, c→c·e) → cv2 (k1×k1, →c2), residual add when shortcut=True and c1 == c2.

whyExists.eli5: The shortcut lets the block only learn what to change, which is easier than learning everything again.
whyExists.simple: The residual shortcut means the block only has to learn a correction, which makes deep networks much easier to train.
whyExists.engineer: Residual learning (He et al.) eases optimisation of deep stacks; stacking two 3×3 convs grows the receptive field by 4 pixels per bottleneck.

eli5: The first helper looks at the notes.
If the shortcut is on, the original notes are added back.
simple: cv1: a Conv (3×3 in C2f, 1×1 in C3).
If shortcut is on and the channel count did not change, the input is added to the output.
engineer: y = x + cv2(cv1(x)) if add else cv2(cv1(x)).
In C2f both kernels are 3×3 and e = 1.0, so hidden width = c.
